content: 1. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of loratadine by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 2. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of losartan by inhibiting metabolism mediated by hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4. This may inhibit the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite, E-3174, potentially reducing its therapeutic effects. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 3. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. However, due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed levels observed with ivacaftor monotherapy at the approved dose of 150 mg every 12 hours. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients on strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily (lumacaftor 200 mg/ivacaftor 125 mg total daily dose) for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. After this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. 4. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole by inducing metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of lumateperone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the lumateperone dose to 5 mg/day. 6. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of lumefantrine by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Both lumefantrine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of maraviroc by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of marijuana by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of mavoryxafor by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Both mavoryxafor and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Mavoryxafor may cause concentration-dependent QTc prolongation, and dose reduction or discontinuation may be required in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. 10. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of methadone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Increased methadone levels have been associated with toxicity, including QT prolongation. Frequent monitoring for adverse events and methadone-related toxicity is recommended during co-administration. Both methadone and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of methylprednisolone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of midazolam by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of mifepristone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Do not exceed a mifepristone dose of 300 mg/day for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. This combination may also prolong the QT interval. Use alternatives if available. 14. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of mirvetuximab soravtansine, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Mitotane decreases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole by inducing metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of modafinil by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of mometasone (intranasal) by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Both moxifloxacin and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Nafcillin decreases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole by inducing metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of naloxegol by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Monitor for potential adverse effects if co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of nateglinide by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP2C9/10. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of nefazodone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Nelfinavir increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, but no dosage adjustment is required. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Nevirapine decreases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole by inducing metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Voriconazole also increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of nevirapine by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of nicardipine by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of nilotinib by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Both nilotinib and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of nisoldipine by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Nitisinone increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP2C9/10. Nitisinone inhibits CYP2C9, and caution is advised if CYP2C9 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index are co-administered. 30. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of norethindrone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of norgestrel by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Both nortriptyline and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Both octreotide and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Both ofloxacin and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Both olanzapine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of oliceridine by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 37. Both voriconazole and olodaterol (inhaled) prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of omeprazole by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of osilodrostat by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Both osilodrostat and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Both osimertinib and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes is recommended in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 41. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of ospemifene by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Oxaliplatin increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole through mechanisms not fully understood. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 43. Oxcarbazepine decreases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole by inducing metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 44. Both ozanimod and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 45. Both paliperidone and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of panobinostat by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Reduce the panobinostat starting dose to 10 mg if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of pantoprazole by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of parecoxib by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP2C9/10. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of paricalcitol by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Both paroxetine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Both pasireotide and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 52. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of voriconazole by inducing metabolism mediated by CYP2C9/10. When co-administered with CYP2C9 substrates, the therapeutic effect of these drugs may be altered. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of perampanel by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Both perphenazine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 55. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of phenytoin by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP2C9/10. Conversely, phenytoin decreases voriconazole levels by inducing metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 56. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE exposure, potentially increasing polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Both posaconazole and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are advised. 58. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of praziquantel by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of prednisolone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 60. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of prednisone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 61. Both primaquine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are advised. 62. Both prochlorperazine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 63. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of progesterone (intravaginal gel) by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 64. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of progesterone (micronized) by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 65. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of natural progesterone by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 66. Both promazine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 67. Both promethazine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 68. Both protriptyline and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 69. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of quazepam by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 70. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and/or pharmacological effect of quetiapine by inhibiting metabolism mediated by CYP3A4. Both quetiapine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Caution and monitoring are advised.
